findings.description: The instance user_data exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in plain text. User data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute or from the instance metadata service, leaking long-lived static credentials.
No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 (unauthenticated token-less metadata retrieval) remains enabled, turning any SSRF in the web application into credential theft.
The instance does not specify root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root EBS volume storing OS and application data may be unencrypted at rest.

The instance is launched in aws_subnet.web_subnet which has map_public_ip_on_launch = true, giving it a public IP address and direct internet exposure rather than placing it behind a load balancer in a private subnet.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
Ingress on port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 permits unencrypted HTTP traffic from the entire internet; data in transit is not protected and no TLS listener is configured.
Egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data-exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the compromised host.
The EBS volume attached to the web host is created without encrypted = true, so data stored on it is unencrypted at rest and not protected by a KMS key.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and no encryption or KMS key is configured, so the snapshot data is stored unencrypted.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive network audit logs are stored unencrypted.
No public access block, bucket ACL restriction, or bucket policy is configured for the flow log bucket, risking unintended public or cross-account exposure of network logs.
The log bucket has no access logging or versioning enabled and uses force_destroy = true, so audit records can be deleted or overwritten without trace.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to every instance in the subnet, exposing workloads directly to the internet instead of isolating them in a private network layer.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, expanding internet-facing attack surface.
The VPC's default security group is not explicitly restricted via aws_default_security_group, so it permits all intra-group traffic and any resource attached to it inherits permissive rules.
